## Overview

IMPACTncdEngland includes a robust pipeline for managing input data files
via [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/), a general-purpose open repository hosted
by CERN. This enables:

- **Reproducibility**: DOI-based versioning ensures you always know which data
  version was used
- **Collaboration**: Easy sharing of input datasets across team members
- **Archiving**: Long-term preservation of input data with persistent
  identifiers
- **Version Control**: Track changes to input data over time

The pipeline uses the `zen4R` package to interact with the Zenodo REST API.
It archives whole directories as zip files, whatever the format of the files
inside them (mostly parquet and fst). It can archive both **input data**
(exposure distributions, disease burden, mortality, etc.) and **simulation
outputs** (PARFs, compiled RR tables).

### What is a DOI?

A **Digital Object Identifier (DOI)** is a permanent, unique identifier for a
digital resource. When you publish data on Zenodo, it receives a DOI that will
always resolve to that exact version of the data, even decades later. This is
the standard way to cite research data in academic publications.

Zenodo provides two types of DOIs:

| Type | Example | Resolves to |
|------|---------|-------------|
| **Concept DOI** | `10.5281/zenodo.12345` | Always the *latest* published version |
| **Version DOI** | `10.5281/zenodo.12346` | A *specific* version (immutable) |

Use the **concept DOI** in your code and share it with collaborators. Cite the
**version DOI** in publications for exact reproducibility.

## Prerequisites

### 1. Install Required Packages

The following packages are required (they are not package Imports):

```{r install-packages}
# zen4R is the only Zenodo dependency declared in DESCRIPTION (Suggests).
# httr2 is required for every download, for listing draft files and for the
# server-side file import used by zenodo_resync_simulation(). It is not
# declared in DESCRIPTION, but is normally already installed because gh (a
# package Import) depends on it; installing it explicitly is a harmless
# safeguard.
install.packages(c("zen4R", "httr2"))
```

(`zip` and `digest` are package Imports, and `keyring`, used in
[Option C](#option-c-keyring-r-package-best-for-windows-or-gui-desktops), is
installed with `zen4R`, so none of them needs installing separately.)

### 2. Get a Zenodo Access Token (uploaders only)

> **Downloading the published data needs no account or token.** The IMPACTncd
> England input-data record is public, so `zenodo_connect()` followed by
> `zenodo_download_all()` works anonymously. You only need a token to
> **upload** or **publish** data. If you only want to run the model, skip to
> [Quick Start](#quick-start).

1. Create a Zenodo account at [zenodo.org](https://zenodo.org/)
2. Go to
   [Applications > Personal access tokens](https://zenodo.org/account/settings/applications/tokens/new/)
3. Create a new token with **deposit:write** and **deposit:actions** scopes
4. Save the token securely (see below)

**For testing**, create a separate sandbox account and token at
[sandbox.zenodo.org](https://sandbox.zenodo.org/account/settings/applications/tokens/new/).
Sandbox and production are **completely separate systems** — they do not
share accounts, tokens, or data. See
[Sandbox vs Production](#sandbox-vs-production) for details.

### 3. Secure Token Management

Your Zenodo token grants full access to your Zenodo deposits. **Never commit
tokens to version control!**

The package reads only `ZENODO_TOKEN`, and only when you omit `token`, whether
or not `sandbox = TRUE`. Always pass the sandbox token explicitly as
`token = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN")`. Otherwise, if `ZENODO_TOKEN` is
set, your production token is sent to the sandbox, which rejects it, and the
connection fails; if it is unset, the connection is anonymous and cannot
upload.

#### Option A: `pass` — GPG-Encrypted (Recommended for Linux/macOS)

[`pass`](https://www.passwordstore.org/) is a standard Unix password manager
that stores each secret as a GPG-encrypted file. It works across R sessions
and shell scripts, making it the most unified approach.

**Why `pass` is recommended:**

- Tokens are GPG-encrypted at rest (not plaintext)
- Works in R (via `.Rprofile`) and in shell scripts (CI uses GitHub secrets
  instead)
- `gpg-agent` caches your passphrase so you only unlock once per session
- No extra R packages required

**First-time setup:**

```bash
# 1. Install pass (if not already installed)
# Ubuntu/Debian: sudo apt install pass
# macOS: brew install pass
# RHEL/Rocky: sudo dnf install pass

# 2. Initialise the password store (if you haven't already)
# pass init "your-gpg-key-id"

# 3. Store your Zenodo tokens
pass insert zenodo/production-token
# Enter your production token when prompted

pass insert zenodo/sandbox-token
# Enter your sandbox token when prompted

# 4. Verify
pass show zenodo/production-token
```

**Auto-loading in R sessions:**

Add this to your `~/.Rprofile` so `Sys.getenv("ZENODO_TOKEN")` and
`Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN")` work automatically:

```r
# Load Zenodo tokens from pass (GPG-encrypted) if available
local({
  if (nzchar(Sys.which("pass"))) {
    load_pass <- function(env_var, pass_key) {
      token <- tryCatch(
        system2("pass", c("show", pass_key), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE),
        error = function(e) character(0)
      )
      if (length(token) == 1L && nzchar(token)) {
        args <- list(token)
        names(args) <- env_var
        do.call(Sys.setenv, args)
      }
    }
    load_pass("ZENODO_TOKEN", "zenodo/production-token")
    load_pass("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN", "zenodo/sandbox-token")
  }
})
```

Then in your R code, just use `Sys.getenv()` — no manual token handling:

```r
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token   = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"),
  sandbox = TRUE
)
```

**Docker builds:**

Docker builds need no Zenodo token and never use the data you have downloaded
locally. The images are built in three layers (prerequisite, data, model).
The data layer (`Dockerfile.data.IMPACTncdENGL`) downloads the published
record anonymously at build time, via `docker_setup/download_zenodo_data.R`
(set `ZENODO_CONCEPT_DOI` in `docker_setup/.env` to use another record), and
the model image inherits that data. For the data and model images,
`docker_build_push.sh` builds its context from the files committed at `HEAD`
(`git archive HEAD`), so uncommitted changes and gitignored data are never
included. From `docker_setup/`:

```bash
# Either build the model image on the published data image (nothing is
# downloaded from Zenodo; Docker pulls the data image from Docker Hub instead):
DATA_IMAGE=chriskypri/data.impactncdengl:latest ./docker_build_push.sh Dockerfile.IMPACTncdENGL

# or build every layer locally (each is tagged <name>:local; build only, no push):
./docker_build_push.sh Dockerfile.prerequisite.IMPACTncdENGL
./docker_build_push.sh Dockerfile.data.IMPACTncdENGL   # downloads ~13 GB from Zenodo
./docker_build_push.sh Dockerfile.IMPACTncdENGL
```

Maintainers publish the data layer with `build_push_data.sh`, which always
pushes to Docker Hub and, on `main`, moves the `:latest` tag.

**Manage your stored tokens:**

```bash
# List Zenodo entries
pass ls zenodo/

# Update a token
pass edit zenodo/production-token

# Delete a token
pass rm zenodo/sandbox-token
```

#### Option B: `.Renviron` File (Simple Alternative)

If you prefer not to use `pass`, the `.Renviron` file stores environment
variables that R loads at startup. Tokens are stored in **plaintext**
but the file is protected by filesystem permissions.

```r
# Open .Renviron for editing
usethis::edit_r_environ()
```

Add these lines to the file:

```
ZENODO_TOKEN=your_production_token_here
ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN=your_sandbox_token_here
```

Save and restart R. The tokens are now available via
`Sys.getenv("ZENODO_TOKEN")` and `Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN")`.

**Security considerations:**

- The `.Renviron` file is stored in your home directory (`~/.Renviron`)
- It is **not** in your project folder, so it won't be accidentally committed
  to git
- Set restrictive permissions: `chmod 600 ~/.Renviron` (Linux/macOS)
- Tokens are stored in **plaintext** — use `pass` (Option A) if you need
  encryption at rest

#### Option C: `keyring` R Package (Best for Windows or GUI Desktops)

On desktops with a graphical environment, `keyring` uses the operating
system's secure credential store (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain,
or Linux Secret Service):

```r
# Store the token (you'll be prompted to enter it securely)
keyring::key_set("zenodo", "token")

# Retrieve the token in your scripts
token <- keyring::key_get("zenodo", "token")
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(token = token)
```

On servers without a desktop environment, use the **file-based backend**:

```r
kb <- keyring::backend_file$new()
kb$keyring_create("zenodo_keyring")
kb$set("zenodo_sandbox", username = "token", keyring = "zenodo_keyring")
kb$set("zenodo", username = "token", keyring = "zenodo_keyring")

# Retrieve
token <- kb$get("zenodo_sandbox", username = "token", keyring = "zenodo_keyring")
```

#### Security Best Practices

| Do | Don't |
|-----|--------|
| Use `pass` or `keyring` for encrypted storage | Store tokens in plaintext `.env` files |
| Use `.Renviron` with `chmod 600` if not using `pass` | Hardcode tokens in scripts |
| Use separate tokens for sandbox vs production | Share tokens between users |
| Regenerate tokens periodically | Use tokens with excessive permissions |
| Use GitHub secrets for CI workflows | Commit tokens to git |

## Quick Start

> **Run everything in this vignette from the repository root** (the folder
> that holds `global.R` and `inputs/`). `Simulation$new()` records that
> folder, and every `zenodo_*` method that reads or writes local files stops
> with an error if the working directory has changed since; `setwd()` back to
> the root and call the method again.

### Downloading Input Data (New Team Member)

If you're setting up the model for the first time, download the input data
from Zenodo. The published data is **public**, so downloading needs **no
Zenodo account or token** — just connect and download:

```{r download-quickstart}
library(IMPACTncdEngland)

# Create the simulation object. On a fresh copy it warns that input data are
# missing; that is expected before the download.
IMPACTncd <- Simulation$new("./inputs/sim_design.yaml")

# Connect (no token needed for downloading published data); the production
# concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20812409 is the default.
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect()

# Download everything needed to run the model (inputs + PARFs + RR tables,
# about 13 GB). The object reloads its data afterwards and is ready to run.
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_all()
```

For testing the pipeline against the sandbox instead, pass
`token = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"), sandbox = TRUE`
(see [Sandbox vs Production](#sandbox-vs-production)).

### Uploading Input Data (Data Manager)

To share your input data via Zenodo, start from a **fresh** `Simulation`
object. `concept_doi = NULL` does not clear a DOI that an earlier
`zenodo_connect()`, upload or `zenodo_publish()` set on the same object, so
the upload would target that record instead of creating a new one (with
`version` given, as a new version of it, ignoring `title`, `description` and
`creators`):

```{r upload-quickstart}
# Fresh object: no concept DOI or record carried over
IMPACTncd <- Simulation$new("./inputs/sim_design.yaml")

# Connect to sandbox for testing
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token   = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"),
  sandbox = TRUE,
  concept_doi = NULL  # no existing record yet
)

# Upload everything (inputs + simulation outputs) in one call
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_all(
  title       = "IMPACTncd England Input Data",
  description = "Input and simulation data for IMPACTncd England",
  creators    = list(
    list(firstname = "Chris", lastname = "Kypridemos",
         orcid = "0000-0002-0746-9229")
  ),
  version = "1.0.0",
  # skip the intermediate .qs PARF caches (see "Uploading Simulation Outputs")
  simulation_exclude_file_patterns = c("\\.R$", "\\.csv$", "\\.qs$")
)

# Verify upload
IMPACTncd$zenodo_list_files()

# When satisfied, publish (IRREVERSIBLE!)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_publish()
```

## Detailed Usage

### Connecting to Zenodo

The `zenodo_connect()` method creates the object's Zenodo manager if it does
not exist yet, connects to the Zenodo API and sets the concept DOI. When
`sandbox = TRUE`, it defaults to the project's sandbox concept DOI
(`10.5072/zenodo.442996`); otherwise to the published production record
(`10.5281/zenodo.20812409`). With `token` omitted it reads `ZENODO_TOKEN` and,
if that is unset, connects anonymously (enough to download published data):

```{r connect-details}
# Sandbox (for testing) — default concept DOI is set automatically
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token   = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"),
  sandbox = TRUE
)

# Production — the published record is the default; a token is only needed
# to upload or publish
# IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(token = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_TOKEN"))

# archive_dir: where upload archives are built and where downloaded input
# archives are staged (default: a folder under tempdir()). They are deleted
# after a successful upload or extraction, so choose it for disk space
# (about 13 GB), not to keep archives (zenodo_create_archives() leaves its
# archives in place for inspection). It is honoured only by the call that
# creates the object's Zenodo manager: once zenodo_connect(),
# zenodo_create_archives() or zenodo_create_manifest() has run on the object,
# it is ignored. So pass it on the object's first zenodo_connect(), before
# either of the other two.
# IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(archive_dir = "/mnt/large_disk/zenodo_archives")
```

The `progress` argument currently changes nothing but the wording of some log
messages; the package draws no progress bars of its own.

> **Switching records on the same object does not work as you might expect.**
> Every `zenodo_connect()` call sets the concept DOI (to the default unless
> you pass one; `concept_doi = NULL` keeps the previous one), but a record
> that is already loaded stays loaded, and downloads and file listings go on
> using it. To work with a different record, or to create a new one, start
> from a fresh `Simulation` object.

### Uploading Input Data

The `zenodo_upload_inputs()` method creates zip archives from your input
directories and uploads them. With no concept DOI set it creates a new record
(`title`, `description` and `creators` are then required); with a concept DOI
set and a `version` given it creates a new version of that record:

```{r upload-inputs}
# First-time upload (creates a new record). Only on a fresh object connected
# with concept_doi = NULL (see Quick Start): after the sandbox connect above,
# which sets the default sandbox DOI, this would make a new version instead.
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_inputs(
  title       = "IMPACTncd England Input Data",
  description = "Exposure distributions, disease burden, mortality, etc.",
  creators    = list(
    list(firstname = "Chris", lastname = "Kypridemos",
         orcid = "0000-0002-0746-9229")
  ),
  version  = "1.0.0",
  keywords = c("microsimulation", "health", "IMPACTncd", "England"),
  license  = "cc-by-sa-4.0"
)

# Alternatively, upload specific directories only. On an existing record this
# makes a version holding ONLY these directories, because a new version starts
# empty (see "Creating New Versions").
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_inputs(
  directories = c("mortality", "exposure_distributions"),
  version     = "1.0.0",
  title       = "IMPACTncd England Input Data",
  description = "Selected input directories",
  creators    = list(
    list(firstname = "Chris", lastname = "Kypridemos")
  )
)
```

### Uploading Simulation Outputs

After uploading inputs, in the same session and before publishing, you can
add simulation-generated files (PARFs and compiled RR tables) to the **same**
draft. `zenodo_upload_simulation()` uploads to the record the object has
loaded, and a published version cannot take new files:

```{r upload-simulation}
# Upload simulation outputs (parf/ and rr/ directories). The default file
# patterns (\\.R$, \\.csv$) keep the intermediate .qs PARF caches that PARF
# generation leaves in simulation/parf/ (several GB), so exclude them:
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_simulation(
  exclude_file_patterns = c("\\.R$", "\\.csv$", "\\.qs$")
)

# With custom directories
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_simulation(
  simulation_base = "./simulation",
  directories     = c("parf", "rr"),
  exclude_file_patterns = c("\\.R$", "\\.csv$", "\\.qs$")
)
```

`simulation/parf/` can hold several `PARF_<disease>_<hash>/` directories for
one disease (the model removes the old ones only when it regenerates that
PARF without a cached `.qs` file), and all of them for a disease go into the
same `parf_PARF_<disease>.zip`. Remove stale ones before uploading; the simplest
reliable way is `IMPACTncd$del_parfs()` followed by a run, which regenerates
only the PARFs the current design needs (this can take hours).

### Uploading Everything at Once

The `zenodo_upload_all()` convenience method runs `zenodo_upload_inputs()`
and then `zenodo_upload_simulation()` on the same draft. Its file patterns
are split into `input_exclude_file_patterns` and
`simulation_exclude_file_patterns`:

```{r upload-all}
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_all(
  title       = "IMPACTncd England Input Data",
  description = "Complete input and simulation data",
  creators    = list(
    list(firstname = "Chris", lastname = "Kypridemos",
         orcid = "0000-0002-0746-9229")
  ),
  version = "1.0.0",
  simulation_exclude_file_patterns = c("\\.R$", "\\.csv$", "\\.qs$")
)
```

### Creating New Versions

When your input data changes, create a new version of the existing record.
**A new version starts empty**: the files of the previous version are not
carried over. `zenodo_upload_inputs(version = ...)` on its own would
therefore produce a version holding only the input archives, without the
PARF and RR archives that `zenodo_download_all()` expects (and, because the
concept DOI resolves to the latest version, every later download would miss
them). Use `zenodo_upload_all()` to replace everything, or
`zenodo_resync_simulation()` ([below](#re-syncing-simulation-archives-parfs-efficiently))
to replace only simulation archives while carrying the inputs over:

```{r new-version}
# Connect with existing concept DOI (the default is "10.5072/zenodo.442996";
# pass concept_doi = "<your concept DOI>" for your own record)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token   = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"),
  sandbox = TRUE
)

# Upload everything as a new version
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_all(
  version = "1.1.0",
  simulation_exclude_file_patterns = c("\\.R$", "\\.csv$", "\\.qs$")
)

# Check, then publish
IMPACTncd$zenodo_list_files()
IMPACTncd$zenodo_publish()
```

### Re-syncing Simulation Archives (PARFs) Efficiently

Sometimes only the **simulation archives** change while the inputs stay
identical — most commonly when a fix alters the PARF cache-key hash, so the
published PARFs no longer match what the model generates and every user would
regenerate them on first run. Re-uploading the (often many-GB) inputs just to
ship new PARFs is wasteful, so `zenodo_resync_simulation()` publishes a new
version that **re-uploads only the archives of the named simulation
directories** (all of them, changed or not) and carries every other file over
server-side:

```{r resync}
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token   = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"),
  sandbox = TRUE
)

# New version with regenerated PARFs only; inputs are imported server-side.
IMPACTncd$zenodo_resync_simulation(
  version     = "1.0.1",
  directories = "parf",   # which ./simulation/ subdirs to re-sync
  publish     = TRUE      # publishes only if the verify-gate passes
)
```

Internally it (1) creates a new-version draft, (2) imports every file from the
previous version via the InvenioRDM `files-import` action (no input
re-upload), (3) deletes the old target archives from the draft, (4) uploads the
regenerated ones, and (5) **verifies the inputs were preserved and all target
archives uploaded before publishing** — otherwise the draft is left
unpublished and an error is raised. The default `exclude_file_patterns` also
drops the intermediate `.qs` PARF caches (which PARF generation keeps by
default), so only the parquet PARF directories are shipped. Every PARF
directory in `simulation/parf/` is archived, so prune stale ones first (see
[Uploading Simulation Outputs](#uploading-simulation-outputs)). As with any
publish, dry-run on the sandbox first.

### Listing Remote Files

After uploading, verify what's on the server:

```{r list-files}
files <- IMPACTncd$zenodo_list_files()
print(files)
```

This lists the record the object has loaded; pass `concept_doi` to load and
list another one. It also works with draft records (where zen4R's built-in
listing may return empty results): the method falls back to a direct API
query, which needs a token.

### Downloading Input Data

Downloads zip archives from the Zenodo record and extracts them into
`./inputs/`. Every selected input archive is downloaded (about 13 GB for all
of them) and staged in `archive_dir` before any is extracted, even when its
files are already present. Extraction is then **per-file**: by default
missing data files are added and existing files are kept — so a fresh git
clone (whose data directories already exist holding git-tracked `.yaml`/`.R`
files) still receives all the data. Pass `overwrite = TRUE` to replace
existing files.

```{r download-details}
# Directory-level check against every archive on the record. PARF, RR,
# root.zip and *_root_files archives always show as missing (they are not
# extracted as directories under ./inputs), a directory that exists counts
# as present even if its data files are missing, and `directories` is
# currently ignored.
status <- IMPACTncd$zenodo_check_inputs()
print(status)

# Download all input archives; add missing files, keep existing ones
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_inputs()

# Download specific directories (a parent name selects its grouped archives)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_inputs(
  directories = c("mortality", "exposure_distributions")
)

# Replace existing files too (read the warning below first)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_inputs(overwrite = TRUE)
```

> **Careful with `overwrite = TRUE`.** The archives also carry files that are
> tracked in git, as they were when the record was uploaded: `root.zip` holds
> the `inputs/sim_design*.yaml` files, `disease_burden_root_files.zip` the
> `inputs/disease_burden/*.yaml` files, and `mortality.zip` and
> `pop_projections.zip` the scripts (and, for mortality, a design file) in
> those folders (see [Exclude Patterns](#exclude-patterns)). With
> `overwrite = TRUE` they replace your copies, including any edits to
> `inputs/sim_design.yaml`. Back up locally edited design files first;
> afterwards review `git status` and `git diff -- inputs/`, and restore only
> unintended changes with `git restore <file>`.

### Downloading PARF and RR Data

If PARFs and compiled RR tables were uploaded to the same Zenodo record
(via `zenodo_upload_simulation()` or `zenodo_upload_all()`), you can
download them separately:

```{r download-simulation}
# Download pre-computed PARFs and RR tables
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_PARFs_RRs()

# Download only PARF files (skip RR)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_PARFs_RRs(directories = "parf")

# Force re-download (overwrites existing)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_PARFs_RRs(overwrite = TRUE)
```

This is useful when:

- A colleague has already generated PARFs/RR tables and you want to reuse
  them instead of re-running the generation step (which can take hours)
- You're setting up a new machine and want to skip time-consuming
  computation

### Downloading Everything at Once

The `zenodo_download_all()` convenience method downloads both input data
**and** simulation outputs in a single call:

```{r download-all}
# New team member — connect to the published record (no token) and download
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect()
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_all()

# Force re-download everything (read the overwrite warning above first)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_all(overwrite = TRUE)
```

This calls `zenodo_download_inputs()` followed by
`zenodo_download_PARFs_RRs()` internally, then reloads the model's input data
so the object can run straight away. Input data goes to `./inputs/` and
simulation data goes to `./simulation/`.

**Updating to a newer data version.** Downloading only adds or replaces
files; it does not invalidate the caches built from the old data. The cached
PARFs are not keyed on the disease-burden data or the exposure tables, and
the model's own clean-up after an input change removes only the `.qs`
intermediates, not the PARF directories. So when you replace the input data,
replace the PARFs too, from the same record version, and remove the
synthetic populations built from the old data:

```{r update-data-version}
IMPACTncd$del_parfs()                            # remove every cached PARF
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_all(overwrite = TRUE)  # new inputs, PARFs and RRs
# (overwrite = TRUE also replaces git-tracked files; see the warning above.)
# Then delete the synthpops built from the old data. del_synthpops() deletes
# EVERYTHING in synthpop_dir, so never use it on a shared folder; a dedicated
# synthpop_dir for experiments is safer.
```

## Advanced: Archive Control

### Exclude Patterns

Control which directories and files are included in archives:

```{r exclude-patterns}
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_inputs(
  version = "1.0.0",
  title   = "...", description = "...", creators = list(...),

  # Skip entire directories matching these regex patterns
  exclude_patterns = c(
    "^unprocessed$",  # Exact match: skip "unprocessed" directory
    "_backup$",       # Ends with "_backup"
    "_old$",          # Ends with "_old"
    "scripts$",       # Ends with "scripts"
    "validation$",    # Ends with "validation"
    "^RR$"            # Source RR .csvy files — tracked in git, not Zenodo
  ),

  # Skip LOOSE files matching these regex patterns (see the caveat below)
  exclude_file_patterns = c(
    "\\.R$",     # R scripts
    "\\.Rmd$",   # R Markdown files
    "\\.yaml$",  # YAML config files
    "\\.html$"   # HTML reports
  )
)
```

The default exclude patterns are designed for the IMPACTncd project:

- **Directory patterns**: `^unprocessed$`, `_backup$`, `_old$`, `scripts$`,
  `validation$`, `^RR$`
- **Input file patterns**: `\\.R$`, `\\.Rmd$`
- **Simulation file patterns**: `\\.R$`, `\\.csv$` (`zenodo_resync_simulation()`
  adds `\\.qs$`)

Both kinds of pattern act only while the pipeline decides **what** to
archive: `exclude_patterns` skips top-level directories and grouped
subfolders, and `exclude_file_patterns` skips loose files lying directly in
`inputs/` or in a directory whose subfolders are grouped. Once a directory is
archived, everything below it goes in, including files that match
`exclude_file_patterns` and, when every subfolder of a directory is excluded
(as `inputs/pop_projections/unprocessed/` is), that subfolder too. The
published `mortality.zip`, for example, contains the git-tracked `.R` scripts
and `sim_design_mrtl_clbr.yaml` of `inputs/mortality/`, and the `file_count`
reported for an archive counts only the files that pass the patterns.

`^RR$` excludes the `inputs/RR/` directory because the source `.csvy`
relative-risk files are **tracked in git** (see `.gitignore` allow-list
`!inputs/RR/**/*.csvy`), not uploaded to Zenodo. The compiled RR `.fst`
files in `simulation/rr/` are still uploaded to Zenodo via
`zenodo_upload_simulation()`.

### Group-By-Prefix

When `group_by_prefix = TRUE` (the default), the subfolders of a directory
that share a prefix (everything before their last underscore) are combined
into a single archive, and the loose files of that directory go into a
separate `<directory>_root_files.zip`. This reduces the number of individual
uploads:

```
inputs/disease_burden/
  ├── af_dur/         ─┐
  ├── af_ftlt/        ─┤── disease_burden_af.zip
  ├── af_incd/        ─┤
  ├── af_prvl/        ─┘
  ├── chd_dur/        ─┐
  ├── chd_ftlt/       ─┤── disease_burden_chd.zip
  ├── ...             ─┘
  ├── 0-scripts/      ─── (excluded: matches "scripts$")
  └── *.yaml          ─── disease_burden_root_files.zip
```

Set `group_by_prefix = FALSE` to create one archive per top-level directory
instead (every file under it, loose files included, goes into that archive).

Zenodo allows at most 100 files per record (an external Zenodo policy at the
time of writing). Only `zenodo_upload_inputs()`, and so the inputs half of
`zenodo_upload_all()`, checks this before uploading, and it counts the files
already on the draft plus the new input archives only.
`zenodo_upload_simulation()` and `zenodo_resync_simulation()` do not check
it, so keep inputs plus simulation archives under 100 yourself. The current
record has 91 files: 68 input archives, 22 `parf_PARF_*.zip` and `rr.zip`.

### Compression Level

The `compression_level` parameter controls the zip compression level (0-9):

| Level | Speed | Size | Use case |
|-------|-------|------|----------|
| 0 | Fastest | Largest | Already-compressed files (parquet, fst) |
| 6 | Balanced | Medium | **Default** — good for most data |
| 9 | Slowest | Smallest | When bandwidth is limited |

```{r compression}
# Fast archiving for pre-compressed files
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_inputs(
  ...,
  compression_level = 0  # store only, no compression
)
```

### Parallel Archive Creation

Archives are created in parallel by default using PSOCK clusters (which are
safe on all platforms, unlike forking). The number of cores defaults to
`clusternumber` from your simulation design YAML:

```{r parallel}
# Use specific number of cores
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_inputs(
  ...,
  multicore = TRUE,
  n_cores   = 10L
)

# Disable parallelism (single-threaded)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_inputs(
  ...,
  multicore = FALSE
)
```

### Preview Archives Before Uploading

Create archives without uploading to inspect sizes and contents. They stay in
`archive_dir`, and `update_gitignore` defaults to `FALSE` here:

```{r preview-archives}
# Create archives locally (no Zenodo connection needed)
archives <- IMPACTncd$zenodo_create_archives()

# Inspect results (file_count counts only the files that pass
# exclude_file_patterns; see "Exclude Patterns")
print(archives[, .(
  archive    = basename(archive_path),
  size_mb    = round(size_bytes / 1024^2, 1),
  file_count = file_count
)])
```

### Automatic Git Tracking Management

When `update_gitignore = TRUE` (the default for the upload methods), two
things happen automatically:

1. **`.gitignore` update** — Every file inside an archived directory that
   does not match `exclude_file_patterns` (not only data files) and is not
   ignored already is added to `.gitignore`, using directory/extension
   patterns where two or more files share them (e.g.,
   `inputs/mortality/*.fst`). Loose files archived into `root.zip` or
   `*_root_files.zip` are not touched.

2. **Git index cleanup** — Any of those files that were *already tracked* by
   git are removed from the git index via `git rm --cached`. This is needed
   because `.gitignore` only prevents *new* untracked files from being staged;
   files that were previously committed continue to be tracked regardless of
   `.gitignore` rules. The `--cached` flag means files are **kept on disk** —
   only the git tracking is removed.

With the default patterns this also untracks the git-tracked configuration
file `inputs/mortality/sim_design_mrtl_clbr.yaml`; committing that change
would remove it from the repository for everyone. After an upload, check
`git status`, and for anything that is not data run
`git restore --staged <file>` and delete its new `.gitignore` line (or add
`"\\.yaml$"` to the file patterns before uploading).

After uploading to Zenodo, your data files live in two places: on your local
disk (for the model to use) and on Zenodo (for reproducibility and sharing).
Anyone cloning the repository will need to run `zenodo_download_all()` (or
`zenodo_download_inputs()` and `zenodo_download_PARFs_RRs()`) to get the
data files.

## Input Directory Structure

With the defaults (`group_by_prefix = TRUE`), the pipeline turns the
directories below into these archives (names as on the published record):

```
inputs/
├── exposure_distributions/    -> exposure_distributions_<prefix>.zip
│   ├── bmi/                      (exposure_distributions_bmi.zip)
│   ├── smok_cig_curr/            (with smok_cig_ex/:
│   ├── smok_cig_ex/               exposure_distributions_smok_cig.zip)
│   └── 0-scripts/                (excluded)
├── disease_burden/            -> disease_burden_<disease>.zip
│   ├── af_dur/ af_incd/ ...      (disease_burden_af.zip)
│   └── *.yaml                    (disease_burden_root_files.zip)
├── mortality/                 -> mortality.zip (no subfolders: archived whole)
├── pop_estimates_lsoa/        -> pop_estimates_lsoa_LSOA_<...>.zip
│   ├── LSOA_mid_year_population_estimates/
│   ├── LSOA_1st_April_population_estimates/
│   └── *.fst                     (pop_estimates_lsoa_root_files.zip)
├── pop_projections/           -> pop_projections.zip (archived whole)
├── aux_data/                  -> aux_data.zip
├── RR/                        (NOT archived — tracked in git instead;
│   ├── bmi~chd.csvy            see "Two RR locations" note below)
│   └── ...
└── sim_design*.yaml           -> root.zip (loose files in inputs/)

simulation/
├── parf/                      -> parf_PARF_<disease>.zip (grouped by disease)
│   ├── PARF_af_<hash>/           (parquet dataset directory)
│   ├── PARF_af_<hash>.qs         (intermediate cache: exclude it)
│   └── ...
└── rr/                        -> rr.zip
    ├── rr_bmi~chd_l.fst
    ├── rr_bmi~chd_indx.fst
    └── ...
```

Each archive stores paths relative to `inputs/` (or `simulation/`), so
extraction recreates the correct paths.

### Two RR locations

The model uses **two distinct RR directories** with different storage
strategies:

| Location | Contents | Storage |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `inputs/RR/` | Source CSVY files (e.g. `bmi~chd.csvy`) — small, human-readable | **Git** (allow-listed in `.gitignore`) |
| `simulation/rr/` | Compiled `.fst` files generated from the CSVYs (e.g. `rr_bmi~chd_l.fst`, `rr_bmi~chd_indx.fst`) — large, binary | **Zenodo** (via `zenodo_upload_simulation()`) |

This is why `^RR$` is in the default `exclude_patterns` for input uploads:
the source files belong in version control, not Zenodo.

## Sandbox vs Production

Zenodo operates two **completely separate systems**. They do not share
accounts, tokens, data, or DOIs. Understanding this distinction is essential
before uploading or downloading data.

| | Sandbox | Production |
|---|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Development and testing | Permanent archiving and citation |
| **Web UI** | [sandbox.zenodo.org](https://sandbox.zenodo.org/) | [zenodo.org](https://zenodo.org/) |
| **Account** | Separate registration required | Separate registration required |
| **Token env var** | `ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN` (pass it as `token =`; the package never reads it itself) | `ZENODO_TOKEN` (read automatically when `token` is omitted) |
| **DOI prefix** | `10.5072/zenodo.XXXXXX` | `10.5281/zenodo.XXXXXX` |
| **Data permanence** | Periodically wiped — records may disappear | Permanent — published records cannot be deleted |
| **Publishable** | Yes, but DOIs do not resolve publicly | Yes — DOIs are globally resolvable and citable |
| **R flag** | `sandbox = TRUE` | `sandbox = FALSE` (default) |

### DOI Prefixes

The DOI prefix tells you instantly which system a record belongs to:

- **`10.5072/zenodo.442996`** — This is a **sandbox** DOI: use it with
  `sandbox = TRUE`. Downloading its published versions needs no token;
  uploading or publishing needs the sandbox token.
- **`10.5281/zenodo.20812409`** — This is a **production** DOI: use it with
  `sandbox = FALSE` (the default). Downloading needs no token; uploading or
  publishing needs the production token.

A sandbox DOI will **not** resolve on production Zenodo and vice versa.
Using a sandbox DOI without `sandbox = TRUE` will give a "Record not
found" error.

### When to Use Each

**Use sandbox** when you are:

- Testing the upload/download pipeline for the first time
- Experimenting with archive settings (compression, grouping, exclusions)
- Developing or debugging Zenodo integration code
- Running CI tests that exercise the Zenodo workflow

**Use production** when you are:

- Sharing input data with collaborators who need to run the model
- Publishing a version of the data alongside a paper or report
- Setting up a reproducible workflow that must persist long-term

### Connecting to Sandbox

When `sandbox = TRUE`, the project's sandbox concept DOI
(`10.5072/zenodo.442996`) is set automatically:

```{r sandbox}
# Sandbox — concept DOI defaults to 10.5072/zenodo.442996
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token   = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"),
  sandbox = TRUE
)

# Override the default sandbox DOI if needed (on an object that has not yet
# loaded a record; see "Connecting to Zenodo")
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token       = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"),
  sandbox     = TRUE,
  concept_doi = "10.5072/zenodo.999999"
)
```

### Connecting to Production

Production is the default. `zenodo_connect()` with no arguments uses the
published IMPACTncd England input-data concept DOI
(`10.5281/zenodo.20812409`) and, unless `ZENODO_TOKEN` is set, connects
anonymously (no token needed to download published data):

```{r production-connect}
# Simplest: defaults to the published production record, no token
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect()

# Equivalent, being explicit (and supplying a token if you also want to
# upload/publish):
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token       = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_TOKEN"),
  concept_doi = "10.5281/zenodo.20812409"
)
```

### Transitioning from Sandbox to Production

Once you have validated your upload/download workflow on sandbox, follow
these steps to move to production:

**1. Create a production Zenodo account and token**

Go to [zenodo.org](https://zenodo.org/account/settings/applications/tokens/new/)
and create a personal access token with `deposit:write` and
`deposit:actions` scopes. Store it as `ZENODO_TOKEN` (see
[Secure Token Management](#secure-token-management) above).

**2. Upload to production (first time — creates a new record)**

Use a fresh `Simulation` object, so that no DOI or record from the sandbox
tests is carried over:

```{r transition-upload}
IMPACTncd <- Simulation$new("./inputs/sim_design.yaml")  # fresh object

IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token       = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_TOKEN"),
  concept_doi = NULL  # no existing production record yet
)

IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_all(
  title       = "IMPACTncd England Input Data",
  description = "Input and simulation data for IMPACTncd England",
  creators    = list(
    list(firstname = "Chris", lastname = "Kypridemos",
         orcid = "0000-0002-0746-9229")
  ),
  version = "1.0.0",
  simulation_exclude_file_patterns = c("\\.R$", "\\.csv$", "\\.qs$")
)
```

**3. Note your new production concept DOI**

Save it — you will use it for all future connections and share it with
collaborators. With `logs: yes` in the design file it is printed when the
record is created and again when it is published; once published, the
record's Zenodo page shows it too:

```{r transition-doi}
# Creating the record prints, among other messages:
#   Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.NNNN
# zenodo_get_versions() lists only PUBLISHED versions and their VERSION DOIs:
# it is empty until the first publish and never shows the concept DOI.
IMPACTncd$zenodo_get_versions()
```

**4. Verify and publish**

Review the draft on the Zenodo website, then publish. **Publishing is
irreversible** — the DOI becomes permanent and the files cannot be
modified (you can only create new versions).

```{r transition-publish}
IMPACTncd$zenodo_list_files()
IMPACTncd$zenodo_publish()
```

**5. Share with collaborators**

Collaborators now download from production using your concept DOI; no token
is needed once the record is published:

```{r transition-download}
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  concept_doi = "10.5281/zenodo.NNNN"  # the concept DOI noted in step 3
)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_all()
```

The concept DOI always resolves to the latest published version, so
collaborators automatically get the most recent data when they download.

## The ZenodoAssetManager Class

Under the hood, the Simulation class delegates to a `ZenodoAssetManager`
R6 class. You can use it directly for more control. It does not check the
working directory: its relative paths (`./inputs`, `./simulation/...`)
resolve against wherever R is when each method runs.

```{r direct-manager}
library(IMPACTncdEngland)

# Create manager directly
zam <- ZenodoAssetManager$new(
  hash_file = "./simulation/zenodo_manifest.csv",
  logs      = TRUE,
  sandbox   = TRUE
)

# Connect and set the concept DOI
zam$connect(token = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"))
zam$set_concept_doi("10.5072/zenodo.442996")

# Get record info (the latest PUBLISHED version)
zam$get_record()
print(zam$record)

# List remote files
files <- zam$list_remote_files()
print(files)

# Create archives with full control
archives <- zam$create_input_archives(
  input_base            = "./inputs",
  directories           = c("mortality", "exposure_distributions"),
  exclude_patterns      = c("^unprocessed$"),
  exclude_file_patterns = c("\\.R$", "\\.Rmd$"),
  group_by_prefix       = TRUE,
  compression_level     = 6L,
  multicore             = TRUE,
  n_cores               = 10L,
  update_gitignore      = FALSE  # TRUE also edits .gitignore and the git index
)

# Uploads need a DRAFT: the published record loaded above cannot take files.
# A new version starts EMPTY, so carry the previous files over and drop the
# ones being replaced, or the published version would hold only these archives.
zam$create_new_version("1.1.0")
zam$import_previous_files()   # server-side copy, no re-upload
# upload_archives() skips names already on the draft, so delete the old copies
zam$delete_draft_files(basename(archives$archive_path))
zam$upload_archives(archives$archive_path)  # verify-and-resume
zam$list_remote_files()                     # check before publishing
# zam$publish_record()                      # IRREVERSIBLE
```

For a brand-new record, call `zam$create_new_record(title, description,
creators)` and then `zam$upload_archives(...)`.

## Hash Manifests

The pipeline uses file hashes (xxhash64) to detect changes:

```{r manifests}
# Hash manifest of the input data files (.parquet, .fst, .csv, .csvy and .yaml
# by default; other files are not hashed). save = TRUE would write
# ./simulation/zenodo_manifest.csv, which every input upload
# (zenodo_upload_inputs() or zenodo_upload_all()) overwrites with an
# archive-level manifest, so keep it FALSE here.
manifest <- IMPACTncd$zenodo_create_manifest(save = FALSE)
print(manifest)

# The ZenodoAssetManager also provides lower-level manifest operations. Keep a
# baseline in its own file and compare against it later:
zam <- ZenodoAssetManager$new()
baseline_file <- "./simulation/inputs_hash_baseline.csv"
zam$save_manifest(zam$compute_manifest("./inputs"), path = baseline_file)

# ... later, after changing some inputs:
diff <- zam$compare_manifests(
  zam$compute_manifest("./inputs"),
  zam$load_manifest(baseline_file)
)
print(diff$modified)  # Files that changed
print(diff$added)     # New files
print(diff$removed)   # Deleted files

# Pass file_patterns to compute_manifest() to hash other file types too.
```

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

**1. "Not connected to Zenodo"**

```r
# Solution: Call zenodo_connect() first
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect()  # production; for the sandbox pass
                            # token = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"), sandbox = TRUE
```

**2. "... requires a Zenodo token, but the manager is connected anonymously"**

Downloading works anonymously, but uploading/publishing needs a token.
Reconnect with a token:

```r
# Solution: pass the token directly (store it as described in
# "Secure Token Management")
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(token = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_TOKEN"))
# (use ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN and sandbox = TRUE for the sandbox)
```

**3. "Record not found for DOI"**

Check that the `sandbox` flag matches the DOI prefix (`10.5072` = sandbox,
`10.5281` = production) and that you passed the concept DOI, not a URL:

```r
# Correct: "10.5072/zenodo.442996"
# Wrong:   "https://doi.org/10.5072/zenodo.442996"
IMPACTncd$zenodo_set_doi("10.5072/zenodo.442996")
```

**4. HTTP 403 Forbidden on file listing**

This can happen when zen4R's internal URL does not match the Zenodo server.
The `list_remote_files()` method automatically falls back to a direct API
query. If you still get 403, ensure your token has the correct scopes
(`deposit:write`, `deposit:actions`).

**5. Empty file listing after upload**

zen4R's `listFiles(pretty = TRUE)` can return empty results for **draft**
records on the new Zenodo InvenioRDM backend. The `zenodo_list_files()` method
handles this automatically by falling back to a direct API query to
`/api/records/{id}/draft/files`, which needs a token (draft files are not
visible anonymously).

**6. "Missing publisher field required for DOI registration"**

This error occurs when publishing. The `publisher` metadata field is required
by Zenodo's InvenioRDM backend for DOI registration. It defaults to
`"Zenodo"` in `zenodo_upload_inputs()`, `zenodo_upload_all()` and
`ZenodoAssetManager$create_new_record()`, so this should arise only for a
draft created outside the package (on the Zenodo website or with zen4R
directly). Setting it on the local record object is not enough: push the
metadata to the draft before publishing.

```r
# Fix (direct manager `zam`): set the publisher, update the server-side draft,
# then publish
zam$record$setPublisher("Zenodo")
zam$record <- zam$zenodo$depositRecord(zam$record, publish = FALSE)
zam$publish_record()
```

**7. Upload shows progress but fails silently**

zen4R may show "No bucket link" warnings and `x` markers during upload, but
the files may actually be uploaded successfully. The upload methods check the
remote file list afterwards, retry missing archives, and stop with
"Upload incomplete" if any is still missing, leaving the draft unpublished.
Re-running `zenodo_upload_simulation()` in the same session resumes it
(archives already on the draft are skipped); re-running
`zenodo_upload_inputs()` or `zenodo_upload_all()` with `version` asks Zenodo
for a new version again rather than resuming, so check the draft with
`zenodo_list_files()` first. `zam$upload_archive()` does not check, so after
using it directly verify with `zam$list_remote_files()`.

**8. An error saying the working directory has changed**

A `zenodo_*` method that reads or writes local files was called from a
different folder from the one `Simulation$new()` recorded (the repository
root). The message names both folders; `setwd()` back to the root and call
the method again.

### Network Issues

For slow connections or large files:

```r
# Download specific directories first (start with smaller ones)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_inputs(
  directories = c("mortality", "aux_data")  # small archives first
)
```

## Complete Example Workflow

### Step 1: Test on Sandbox

Before committing to permanent production records, validate your workflow
on sandbox:

```{r workflow-sandbox-test}
library(IMPACTncdEngland)

# 1. Create simulation object
IMPACTncd <- Simulation$new("./inputs/sim_design.yaml")

# 2. Connect to sandbox (no existing record)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token       = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"),
  sandbox     = TRUE,
  concept_doi = NULL  # creates a new sandbox record
)

# 3. (Optional) Preview archives first
archives <- IMPACTncd$zenodo_create_archives()
print(archives[, .(archive = basename(archive_path),
                    size_mb = round(size_bytes / 1024^2, 1))])

# 4. Upload everything
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_all(
  title       = "IMPACTncd England Input Data",
  description = paste(
    "Input and simulation data for the IMPACTncd England",
    "microsimulation model, including exposure distributions,",
    "disease burden estimates, mortality data, PARFs, and",
    "compiled relative risk tables."
  ),
  creators = list(
    list(firstname = "Chris", lastname = "Kypridemos",
         orcid = "0000-0002-0746-9229")
  ),
  version = "1.0.0",
  simulation_exclude_file_patterns = c("\\.R$", "\\.csv$", "\\.qs$")
)

# 5. Verify — check file count and sizes look correct
files <- IMPACTncd$zenodo_list_files()
cat("Uploaded", nrow(files), "files\n")

# 6. Publish sandbox record (safe — sandbox records are not permanent)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_publish()

# 7. Confirm the round trip from a FRESH clone of the repository, not from
#    this working tree (overwrite = TRUE here would replace git-tracked files;
#    see "Downloading Input Data"). In the clone, from its root, with the
#    concept DOI of the new sandbox record:
#    IMPACTncd <- Simulation$new("./inputs/sim_design.yaml")
#    IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(token = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN"),
#                             sandbox = TRUE,
#                             concept_doi = "10.5072/zenodo.NNNN")
#    IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_all()
```

### Step 2: Publish to Production

Once you're confident the pipeline works, repeat on production from a fresh
`Simulation` object (the sandbox object still holds the sandbox DOI and
record). This creates a **permanent, citable record** — the DOI cannot be
retracted.

```{r workflow-production}
# Fresh object, then connect to production (no existing record)
IMPACTncd <- Simulation$new("./inputs/sim_design.yaml")
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token       = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_TOKEN"),
  concept_doi = NULL  # first upload — creates a new production record
)

# Upload (same parameters as sandbox)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_all(
  title       = "IMPACTncd England Input Data",
  description = paste(
    "Input and simulation data for the IMPACTncd England",
    "microsimulation model, including exposure distributions,",
    "disease burden estimates, mortality data, PARFs, and",
    "compiled relative risk tables."
  ),
  creators = list(
    list(firstname = "Chris", lastname = "Kypridemos",
         orcid = "0000-0002-0746-9229")
  ),
  version = "1.0.0",
  simulation_exclude_file_patterns = c("\\.R$", "\\.csv$", "\\.qs$")
)

# Verify upload
files <- IMPACTncd$zenodo_list_files()
cat("Uploaded", nrow(files), "files\n")

# IMPORTANT: Save your concept DOI before publishing!
# You will need it for all future connections. With logs: yes it was printed
# as "Concept DOI: ..." when the record was created; zenodo_get_versions()
# cannot show it.

# Publish (IRREVERSIBLE — the DOI becomes permanent)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_publish()
```

### New Team Member (Downloading Data)

Share your **production concept DOI** with collaborators. They download
with no token:

```{r workflow-download}
library(IMPACTncdEngland)
IMPACTncd <- Simulation$new("./inputs/sim_design.yaml")

# Connect to production with the project's concept DOI (the default)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  concept_doi = "10.5281/zenodo.20812409"
)

# Download everything (inputs + pre-computed PARFs + RR tables)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_all()

# Or download only inputs (if you want to generate PARFs/RR yourself)
# IMPACTncd$zenodo_download_inputs()

# Run simulation (see vignette("how_to_test_run"))
IMPACTncd$run(mc = 1:10, multicore = TRUE, scenario_nam = "sc0")
```

### Publishing Updated Data (New Version)

When input data changes, create a new version of the **existing**
production record. A new version starts empty, so upload everything (or use
`zenodo_resync_simulation()` when only simulation archives changed):

```{r workflow-update}
# Connect with existing production concept DOI
IMPACTncd$zenodo_connect(
  token       = Sys.getenv("ZENODO_TOKEN"),
  concept_doi = "10.5281/zenodo.20812409"  # your production concept DOI
)

# Upload as new version (inputs + simulation archives)
IMPACTncd$zenodo_upload_all(
  version = "1.1.0",
  simulation_exclude_file_patterns = c("\\.R$", "\\.csv$", "\\.qs$")
)

# Verify and publish
IMPACTncd$zenodo_list_files()
IMPACTncd$zenodo_publish()

# Check version history
IMPACTncd$zenodo_get_versions()
```

## API Reference

### Simulation Class Methods

All of these except `zenodo_set_doi()`, `zenodo_publish()`,
`zenodo_list_files()` and `zenodo_get_versions()` check the working directory
first, and stop with an error if it has changed since `Simulation$new()`.

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `zenodo_connect(token, concept_doi, sandbox, archive_dir, progress)` | Connect to Zenodo and set the concept DOI (`archive_dir` is used only if this call creates the object's Zenodo manager; `progress` currently has no effect) |
| `zenodo_set_doi(concept_doi)` | Change the concept DOI before any record is loaded (an already-loaded record keeps being used; create a fresh Simulation object to switch records) |
| `zenodo_check_inputs(input_base, directories)` | Directory-level check of local vs remote archives (`directories` is currently ignored) |
| `zenodo_download_inputs(input_base, directories, overwrite)` | Download and extract input archives |
| `zenodo_download_PARFs_RRs(simulation_base, directories, overwrite)` | Download and extract simulation archives |
| `zenodo_download_all(input_base, input_directories, simulation_base, simulation_directories, overwrite)` | Download inputs + simulation in one call, then reload the data |
| `zenodo_upload_inputs(input_base, ..., publish)` | Create archives and upload inputs |
| `zenodo_upload_simulation(simulation_base, directories, ...)` | Upload simulation outputs (PARF, RR) to the loaded draft |
| `zenodo_upload_all(input_base, simulation_base, ..., publish)` | Upload inputs + simulation in one call |
| `zenodo_resync_simulation(version, directories, ..., publish)` | New version re-uploading ONLY changed simulation archives (e.g. PARFs); imports unchanged inputs server-side |
| `zenodo_publish()` | Publish the draft record (**irreversible!**) |
| `zenodo_list_files(concept_doi)` | List all files in the loaded record (or in the record of `concept_doi`) |
| `zenodo_get_versions()` | List published versions and their version DOIs |
| `zenodo_create_archives(input_base, ...)` | Create archives locally (no upload) |
| `zenodo_create_manifest(input_base, save)` | Create a file hash manifest (`save = TRUE` overwrites `./simulation/zenodo_manifest.csv`) |

### Archive Creation Parameters

These parameters are available in `zenodo_upload_inputs()` and
`zenodo_create_archives()`. `zenodo_upload_all()` takes the same set, except
that the file patterns are split into `input_exclude_file_patterns` (default
`c("\\.R$", "\\.Rmd$")`) and `simulation_exclude_file_patterns` (default
`c("\\.R$", "\\.csv$")`):

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `exclude_patterns` | `c("^unprocessed$", "_backup$", "_old$", "scripts$", "validation$", "^RR$")` | Regex patterns for directories to skip |
| `exclude_file_patterns` | `c("\\.R$", "\\.Rmd$")` | Regex patterns for loose files to skip (see [Exclude Patterns](#exclude-patterns)) |
| `group_by_prefix` | `TRUE` | Combine subdirectories by shared prefix |
| `compression_level` | `6` | Zip compression (0=store, 9=max) |
| `multicore` | `TRUE` | Parallel archive creation |
| `n_cores` | `clusternumber` from YAML | Number of CPU cores |
| `update_gitignore` | `TRUE` (`FALSE` in `zenodo_create_archives()`) | Auto-update .gitignore and remove tracked files from the git index |
